falsifier: at any of 5, 10 or 20 choices, for any answerer, the potential-first order decides fewer ASVS units in sum over the 32 reports than the band-first order
hypothesis: at 5, 10 and 20 choices, an owner who answers the list from the top decides at least as many ASVS units under the potential-first order as under the band-first order, for every answerer (stated before the run)
intervention: Offline, run.py early-answerers over evals/ at 9fad621e (the code of #1633): 218 archived reports of 11 cases that hold reports of both frameworks (186 STRIDE, 32 ASVS), each read alone and with both frameworks selected; four answerers (yes, no, unknown, alternate by the capability's name), two orders (the shipped potential-first list, and the list with answer_round.capability_effects stubbed to no effect, which is the band-first order), one question a save, read at 5/10/20 choices. ASVS alone, units decided, potential first against band first: no 2,744/3,158 at 5, 3,752/3,680 at 10, 4,022/3,914 at 20; alternate 2,228/2,768, 3,224/3,242, 3,794/3,542; yes 1,094/1,748, 1,700/2,402, 2,660/2,876; unknown 800/800 at every budget. Questions removed under no: 972/840 at 5. Paired by report at 5 choices the potential-first order decides fewer units on 18 (no), 30 (alternate) and 30 (yes) of 32 reports, and more on none. STRIDE alone is identical under both orders.
reconsider_when: the capability catalog, the applicability tables, EARLY_RULES, the effects rule or the order within a framework's turn changes
scope: archived extracted models with no catalog; an owner who answers the first listed question and saves, one question a save; counts of dependency sets completed and units decided, not findings an answer changes; no holdout case read
signature: the adaptive list of #1632 ranks a question by the most other questions an answer removes, and nothing says whether that order decides more applicability units at matched choices than the band-and-units order of ADR 0055

falsifier: at any of 5, 10 or 20 choices, for any answerer, STRIDE with both frameworks selected completes fewer than 80% of the findings it completes alone
hypothesis: once the turns start from what the saved answers charged each framework, STRIDE completes at least 80% of its alone figure at 5, 10 and 20 choices with ASVS beside it, for every answerer (stated before the rerun)
intervention: The first reading (early-answerers.json) showed STRIDE completing 45, 96 and 830 findings at 5, 10 and 20 choices with both selected, against 946, 1,488 and 1,939 alone. answer_round.recommended now passes by_turn the choices the saved answers charged each framework. run.py early-answerers --selections all at the fix (early-answerers-all-after.json): STRIDE completes 929, 1,342 and 1,958 (critical or high 538, 728, 1,015), the same under both orders at 5 and 10 choices and for every answerer at 5 and 10. ASVS with both selected decides fewer units than before the fix at each budget (no, band first: 3,158 to 1,898 at 5 choices), because the choices are shared.
reconsider_when: the turn rule, EARLY_RULES or the list's selection changes
scope: as E1; the alone figures are unchanged by the fix and were not rerun
signature: with both frameworks selected, an owner who answers the list from the top one question a save meets the ASVS question first on every build, because the frameworks' turns start from zero charge on each build and not from the saved answers

falsifier: the p95 of 20 builds with nothing kept is 500 ms or more on either model, with or without thirty answers
hypothesis: caching key_ref, reading a unit's band once in open_capability_needs, and keeping early_questions and capability_effects by a digest of what they read bring the p95 of a build with nothing kept under 500 ms on both models (stated before the measurement)
intervention: Measured in one process on an idle machine, 20 builds each, STRIDE and ASVS level 3, before and after the three changes. Before: shared test model p95 574 ms (no answers) and 548 ms (thirty yes answers); largest corpus model (14-loyalty-oauth-platform, 22 elements) 777 ms and 760 ms. After, nothing kept: 169 ms and 305 ms; 180 ms and 332 ms. After, kept: 11 to 14 ms. The page's input feedback (p95 under 100 ms) was not measured.
reconsider_when: the capability catalog, the applicability tables, the memo size or the effects rule changes
scope: one process, one machine, no concurrent requests; the service's build only, not the page's render; a kept read is one whose content digest the memo holds
signature: the question set of #1633 builds in a p95 of 574 ms on the shared test model and 777 ms on the largest corpus model with STRIDE and ASVS level 3, over the 500 ms #1632 proposed for a save and its recalculation

falsifier: at any of 5, 10 or 20 choices, for any answerer, the effects tiebreak decides more than 1% fewer ASVS units in sum over the 32 reports
hypothesis: on the archive, the effects tiebreak decides within 1% as many ASVS units as the depth-and-name tiebreak at 5, 10 and 20 choices for every answerer (stated before the run)
intervention: run.py early-answerers --selections alone at the chosen order (band and units first, the effects as the tiebreak; early-answerers-alone-tiebreak.json), against the list with the effects stubbed (the depth-and-name tiebreak). ASVS alone, units decided, effects tiebreak against depth-and-name: identical at 5 and 20 choices for every answerer (yes 1,748 and 2,876; no 3,158 and 3,914; alternate 2,768 and 3,542); at 10 choices yes 2,384 against 2,402, one unit fewer on 18 of 32 reports, 0.7%; no and alternate identical. Questions removed under no at 5 choices: 936 against 840. STRIDE alone identical.
reconsider_when: the effects rule, the capability catalog or the order within a framework's turn changes
scope: as E1, alone only; the 18-against-7 figure is one small model with many ties at thirty answers, and does not show on the archive
signature: the shipped order breaks a tie between two capabilities of one band and one unit count by what an answer settles, and on the shared test model at ASVS level 2 thirty yes answers leave 18 level 1 units unknown under it against 7 under the depth-and-name tiebreak
